System NPL Ratio: Weighted, Not Averaged

MediumFreeQuerying BasicsAggregation & Grouping

npl_ratio is a bank's non-performing loans as a percentage of its loans. A regulator's dashboard shows the system-wide ratio for each quarter, and whoever built it took the plain average of the banks' ratios — which gives a community bank the same say as one of the largest banks in the country. The system ratio is all non-performing loans divided by all loans: each bank's ratio counted in proportion to its loans (net_loans).

Use the rows that have an npl_ratio and net_loans above 0. Show exactly these 4 columns: period_end, banks, avg_bank_npl_pct (the plain average, rounded to 3 decimals) and system_npl_pct (the loan-weighted ratio, 3 decimals). Order by period_end.

Hint

A bank's non-performing loans in money are its ratio times its loans. Add those up across the banks of a quarter and divide by the quarter's total loans; then the largest banks count in proportion to their size.
